chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding the son of al-mula'ana that his mother inherits one-third, and the remainder belongs to the Imam, because his crime is against the Imam.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These two reports are not acted upon, because we have clarified that the inheritance of the son of al-mula'ana for his mother is all of it, and the reason for both is taqiyyah.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.ابْنُ الْمُلاَعَنَةِ: Son of al-mula'ana (child of a couple undergoing oath of elimination)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for the son of al-mula'ana in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential evolution regarding the 'son of al-mula'ana', contrasting Imam Ali’s ruling of a one-third share for the mother with the remainder for the Imam, against the later scholarly consensus that the mother inherits the entirety. The discrepancy is attributed to *taqiyyah* (prudent dissimulation), reflecting the political sensitivity of the Imam’s direct claim to the father’s portion during periods of imamate. This distinction underscores the Shia method of reconciling early authoritative rulings with later practical applications in inheritance law.
